observations.observation: Both pages have a single h1 and declare lang 'en'. The original's h1 reads 'Home Design Software for DIY'. The AI-built page's h1 reads 'Home design software for DIY users'.

tags.value: kept: single h1 with lang en

observations.observation: The document titles differ. The original is titled 'Home Designer | Home Design Software for DIY' and the AI-built page 'Home Designer Software – DIY Home Design Software'. Both have a meta description and no JSON-LD. The original also has theme-color and google-site-verification meta tags, an iframe and a base tag, which the AI-built page lacks.

tags.value: changed: branded title and extra meta become short title and minimal meta

observations.observation: The h1 is styled differently. The original's h1 is small (27px), light weight (300) and white on a light-blue band. The AI-built page's h1 is large (46px), bold (700) and dark navy rgb(20,55,85) on a pale grey-blue band, wrapping onto two lines.

tags.value: changed: small light white h1 becomes large bold navy two-line h1

observations.observation: Each page uses a single typeface family, but a different one. The original uses the Open Sans webfont (591 elements). The AI-built page uses only a system-ui sans-serif stack (292 elements) and loads no stylesheets.

tags.value: changed: open sans webfont becomes system-ui stack

observations.observation: Heading weight and scale differ. The original sets headings light (300), with h2 at 37px, which is larger than the 27px h1. The AI-built page sets headings bold (700), with h2 at 32px, smaller than the 46px h1.

tags.value: changed: light weight headings become bold size contrast

observations.observation: Body text metrics differ. The original uses 16px text with 24px line height. The AI-built page uses 17px text with 27.2px line height (1.6).

tags.attribute: body text size and line height
tags.value: changed: 16px 1.5 becomes 17px 1.6

observations.observation: The original applies a 'caicon' icon font to 18 elements, and its glyphs render as empty boxes in the search field, buttons, external-link marks and social row. The AI-built page uses no icon font or SVG icons.

tags.value: dropped: icon fonts for social and ui glyphs

observations.observation: Several images on the original fail to load. Broken alt text overlaps the 'Download' heading, and the comparison matrix image shows only alt text in an empty box. All images on the AI-built page render.

tags.value: dropped: broken thumbnail images with alt text

observations.observation: The heroes differ. The original's hero is a centered 1000x563 watercolor-style 3D house render with a play icon and a 'Watch Time Lapse Design Video' caption. The AI-built page's hero is a two-column split: text, badge, buttons and link lists on the left, and a single 260x368 product box image with a soft shadow on the right.

tags.value: changed: centered house render becomes two-column text and product box hero

observations.observation: The brand colors differ. The original's dominant brand color is light sky blue rgb(96,195,231), which fills the intro band, buttons, comparison section and Learn More band. The AI-built page uses a navy-blue family (rgb(31,78,121), rgb(20,55,85)) for buttons, headings, utility bar and footer.

tags.value: changed: light sky blue becomes navy blue family

observations.observation: The secondary background colors differ. The original's most common background is light gray rgb(241,241,241), used on the link strip, products panel and footer. The AI-built page uses a pale grey-blue rgb(243,246,249) for its alternating section bands.

tags.value: changed: light gray becomes pale grey-blue alternating bands

observations.observation: Each page has a single contrasting accent color. The original uses a lime-green panel rgb(159,196,62) behind the Chief Architect product. The AI-built page uses orange rgb(217,130,43) for a promo badge, the label underlines and the checkmarks.

tags.value: changed: lime green panel becomes orange accent

observations.observation: Link styling differs. On the original, inline links are saturated blue rgb(3,151,214) without underline, distinguished by color only. On the AI-built page, body links are underlined blue, and nav and footer links are not underlined.

tags.value: changed: color-only blue links become underlined body links

observations.observation: Body text color differs slightly. The original uses near-black rgb(34,34,34) and the AI-built page uses dark blue-gray rgb(27,39,51).

tags.value: changed: near-black body text becomes dark blue-gray

observations.observation: Both pages are flat. Neither has gradients, backdrop blur, animations or transforms, and each has only 2 box shadows (on the AI-built page, both are on product images).

tags.value: kept: flat with few shadows

observations.observation: Corner radius differs. The original is almost entirely square-cornered (608 at 0px, 1 small radius), and its primary button has a 0px radius. The AI-built page rounds its buttons (6px), cards and badge (12 elements at 1–7px, 14 at 8–15px).

tags.value: changed: square corners become small rounding

observations.observation: Transition use differs. The original uses 21 CSS transitions and the AI-built page uses none.

tags.value: changed: many transitions become none

observations.observation: The headers are arranged differently. The original has a large text logo lockup ('Home Designer® Software by Chief Architect®') at top left, with a search bar and 'All Content' select at top right and pipe-separated My Account | Contact Us | Cart links below the search bar. The AI-built page puts My Account / Contact Us / Cart in a thin dark-navy utility bar above a white header holding a text wordmark (with a <small> 'by Chief Architect®' line) and has no search bar.

tags.value: changed: search and account links become dark navy utility bar
changed: header search bar and select

observations.observation: The primary navigation differs. On the original, it is a row of four plain text items (Products, Project Type, User Center, Support) below the logo. On the AI-built page, it is a horizontal list of 8 plain text items to the right of the wordmark.

tags.value: changed: four items below logo become eight items right of wordmark

observations.observation: The primary call-to-action button differs. The original's is an outlined 'Rent $59/mo.' button with a transparent background, white border and text, 2px 10px padding and 0px radius, set beside a product box shot in the blue intro band. The AI-built page's is a filled navy 'Download Trial Version' button (11px 20px padding, 6px radius) paired with an outlined secondary 'Purchase Software' button.

tags.value: changed: outlined rent button becomes filled navy button plus outline button

observations.observation: The AI-built page repeats a filled-primary / outlined-secondary button pairing throughout (Buy vs Learn More, Go to Shopping Cart vs Upgrades & Discounts). The original's buttons are flat rectangles: blue buy/rent buttons, a white LEARN MORE button and a dark gray Compare Features button.

tags.value: changed: flat rectangles become rounded filled and outline buttons

observations.observation: Both pages have three Download / Explore / Learn link columns with h3 headings. On the original, they form a gray strip below the hero, with centered headings over small blue link lists. On the AI-built page, they sit inside the hero under the CTAs, with small uppercase letter-spaced labels, orange underline accents and underlined blue links.

tags.value: changed: link columns strip becomes links inside hero with eyebrow labels

observations.observation: Both pages skip heading levels. Both outlines go h1 then three h3s (Download/Explore/Learn) before the first h2. The original adds an h4 under an h2 and uses 9 h5s. The AI-built page uses h4 for footer column titles with no h3 above them.

tags.value: kept: skipped heading levels h3 before h2

observations.observation: The content columns differ in width. The original holds text in a centered column of about 970–1000px on the 1440px page. The AI-built page uses a centered column of about 1068px (x=186–1254), with every section aligned to the same left edge.

tags.value: changed: 1000px column becomes centered 1068px column

observations.observation: Both pages arrange content in full-width horizontal bands of alternating background color. The original alternates white, light blue, gray, green and blue bands. The AI-built page alternates white and pale grey-blue bands, ending in a navy footer.

tags.value: changed: multicolor bands become alternating white and pale bands

observations.observation: Both pages show product cards with 130x184 box-shot images at natural size, a product name and struck-through list prices beside sale prices ($129→$99, $249→$199, $595→$495). The original's cards also show upgrade price lines ('Upgrades from $29').

tags.value: kept: product cards with struck-through prices

observations.observation: The product row is arranged differently. The original splits it into two unequal panels: a wide gray panel with three DIY products and a narrower green panel with the Chief Architect product and a white LEARN MORE button. The AI-built page uses a uniform four-column card row, where the fourth (Chief Architect) card has no price and an outlined Learn More button.

tags.value: changed: two unequal panels become uniform four-column card row

observations.observation: On the AI-built page, two-line product names ('Home Designer Architectural', 'Chief Architect Professional Software') push their prices lower than in the one-line cards, while the CTAs stay aligned at the same baseline.

tags.value: added: aligned ctas with uneven name heights

observations.observation: The original has a blue comparison band with a white light-weight 'Home Designer®' h2, a 'Top-rated DIY home design software' h4 subhead and a flat dark gray 'Compare Features' button next to a (broken) comparison matrix image. The AI-built page has no such band. Instead, a bold underlined 'Compare Products →' text link follows the product cards.

tags.value: changed: blue comparison band with matrix image

observations.observation: The AI-built page has a 3x2 grid of bordered, text-only white feature cards (h3 plus grey paragraph, equal height per row, some with inline links). The original has no comparable card grid.

tags.value: added: uniform bordered text-only feature cards

observations.observation: The AI-built page has a two-column 'Why choose Home Designer' block, with a text column holding a checkmark list with orange ✓ bullets and a 280x396 product box image on the right.

tags.value: added: two-column checkmark list with product image

observations.observation: The Learn More sections differ. The original's is a blue band with a large box-shot image on the left, a vertical list of eight black text links in the middle and a white Purchase Options card on the right. The AI-built page's is two columns of four underlined text links on a grey band, with no image.

tags.value: changed: image and link list band becomes two-column text links

observations.observation: Purchase options are presented differently. The original has an interactive card with New/Upgrade tabs and labeled select dropdowns (Product active; Media and Backup Media disabled), built from 8 selects and 3 forms. The AI-built page uses four equal bordered static info boxes with uppercase bold labels (PRODUCT (MAC & PC), MEDIA, BACKUP MEDIA, PRICE DISPLAY) and no form controls.

tags.value: changed: interactive tabbed selects become static info boxes
changed: select dropdowns and forms

observations.observation: The AI-built page uses small uppercase letter-spaced labels as a recurring device: in the hero link columns, the purchase boxes and the footer headings. The original's labels and headings are light-weight mixed case.

tags.value: changed: wide-tracked uppercase eyebrow labels

observations.observation: Both pages use product-focused promotional copy with pricing and superlatives such as 'top-rated'. The original has 733 words, 2 exclamation marks, 3 em dashes and 3 emoji ('Get started on your design project today!'). The AI-built page has 640 words, uses plain declarative sentences and has no exclamations, em dashes or emoji.

tags.value: changed: exclamatory ctas become plain sentences

observations.observation: Both footers have five link columns: Products, Project Type, User Center, Support, Company. The original's footer is gray, with light-weight column headings, small (~12px) links and external-link icons. The AI-built page's footer is navy and 848px tall, with white or pale links, uppercase h4 headings and COMPANY wrapping to a second row.

tags.value: changed: white footer becomes dark navy footer

observations.observation: Both footers end with a row of seven social links. On the original, they are icon glyphs that render as empty boxes. On the AI-built page, they are plain text links (HomeTalk … Pinterest), followed by a hairline divider and a copyright line with inline Terms and Privacy links.

tags.value: changed: icon glyphs become plain text links
changed: copyright line

observations.observation: Both pages are link-dense and use no <button> elements; controls are anchors styled as buttons. The original has 144 anchors and the AI-built page 94, with destinations repeated across nav, body and footer. The original has no ARIA attributes, and the AI-built page has one.

tags.value: kept: styled anchors rather than button elements

observations.observation: The markup differs in structure. The original has no <main> and is built from 118 divs and 10 sections, with 25 scripts, 6 noscript blocks, 6 stylesheets and 9 inline style attributes. The AI-built page uses header, nav, main, 5 sections, a figure and footer, with 48 divs, no scripts, no external stylesheets, one <style> block and 1 inline style attribute.

tags.value: changed: heavy markup becomes minimal markup
changed: generic divs become header nav main sections footer

observations.observation: The layout mechanisms differ. The original uses flex on only 8 elements and no CSS grid. The AI-built page uses 9 grid and 10 flex containers for its feature grid, product row, purchase row and footer columns.

tags.value: changed: flexbox-only becomes flex plus grid columns

observations.observation: Both pages use custom (non-utility) class names, at different volumes. The original has 432 class uses across 148 unique classes, about 8% of them Tailwind-like. The AI-built page has 57 uses across 22 unique classes, none Tailwind-like.

tags.value: changed: custom class names rather than utility classes

observations.observation: The image sets differ in size and content. Both are mostly product box shots with complete alt text. The original has 11 images, including a large 1000x563 watercolor house render and a comparison matrix image. The AI-built page has 6 images, all product box shots, with the 348x492 Professional box shot used twice at scaled sizes.

tags.value: changed: many images become few product box shots

observations.observation: The pages are close in size. Both are 1440px wide. The original is 4284px tall and the AI-built page 4563px.

tags.value: changed: shorter page becomes slightly taller page

observations.observation: The AI-built page sets the hero lead paragraph in muted grey-blue rgb(86,101,116), slightly larger than body text. The original sets its intro paragraph in white on the blue band.

tags.value: changed: white intro text becomes muted grey-blue lead paragraph

observations.observation: On the AI-built page, section h2s share a uniform pattern: left-aligned, navy, about 60px of padding above, consistent vertical rhythm and no decorative dividers.

tags.value: added: left-aligned navy h2 with consistent padding
added: regular gutters and row spacing
